result: Independent verification found a correctness defect: the Lua parser can emit a catalog ID from any matched table containing name=, without requiring type="autoplace-control". Thus a non-control declaration using a manifest ID could be emitted. Backend tests passed 62/62 and dotnet build passed with 0 warnings/errors. Frontend TypeScript noEmit typecheck passed; full build was blocked by EPERM writing node_modules/.tmp, and pnpm attempted an install despite local dependencies.

evidence.outcome: The regex captures name fields but never validates type="autoplace-control"; it therefore cannot guarantee IDs are explicitly declared as autoplace controls.
Exactly five surfaces and explicit manifest routing are enforced; unknown IDs are omitted.
Base and Space Age files are selected from the requested version and enabled Space Age state; custom enabled mod prototype directories are not scanned and are safely omitted.
Known overrides are normalized and legacy fields are mapped, but unknown override dictionary entries remain persisted even though serialization omits them.
Catalog controls are written only to autoplace_controls in map-gen settings; enemy evolution and expansion are written only to map-settings.
GET catalog and PUT settings return a bad request when active version or declarations are unavailable.
CreateSaveAsync writes the effective mod list before resolving the catalog and uses the same settings-derived catalog for map generation.
TypeScript noEmit typecheck passed; full build could not run because tsc -b was denied writing node_modules/.tmp/tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo.

next_slice.summary: Fix the catalog parser to accept only tables explicitly declaring type="autoplace-control", add a regression test for non-control tables, and optionally filter unknown ControlOverrides during normalization. Re-run backend and frontend builds in an environment where local build cache writes are permitted.

knowledge_proposal: The parser must validate prototype type, not only name, before emitting catalog entries.
blockers: Full frontend build was blocked by EPERM writing node_modules/.tmp; no dependency installation was performed intentionally.
